title: Two Records in an Afternoon on the Lisbon Coast
title_candidates: Two Records in an Afternoon on the Lisbon Coast
Praia D'El Rey Gives Up Its Secrets Immediately
The Best Round Ever Recorded, on Day One
theme: TEG's first visit to Praia D'El Rey produced the two best rounds in its history on the same afternoon, and a scoreboard already pulling in two directions.
opening_hook: Six men arrived at a course none of them had ever seen, on a coastline TEG had never visited, and by teatime two of them had posted the best net round and the best gross round in the tournament's history — the other four, meanwhile, were counting eights.

round_story.subject: Henry Meller's -13 at Praia D'El Rey, the best round in TEG history to date, built on a back nine of almost total serenity after an early wobble and a nine at the 8th
round_story.why_it_matters: It is rank one of 101 rounds ever played in TEG, and it came on a course nobody in the field had walked before; it also gave Meller the outright Trophy lead at -13.
round_story.shape: Meller opens with three straight pars for four shots to par in three holes and looks unbothered, then the run ends with a double bogey at the 4th and a nine at the par-five 8th, the hardest hole on the card. From the 10th he simply stops making mistakes — nine holes, seven pars, two bogeys, ten more shots to par — and finishes with a gross +12 that is the best round of his own career. The result is -13, the lowest net-vs-par round TEG has recorded, and a three-shot Trophy lead after one day.
headline_candidates: Meller Posts the Best Round in TEG History
Nine Holes That Rewrote the Record
Meller Answers a Nine With Serenity
round_story.chosen_headline: Meller Posts the Best Round in TEG History
round_story.standfirst: A quadruple-bogey nine at the par-five 8th should have ended it; instead he played the closing nine in ten shots to par and set a personal-best gross into the bargain.

race_story.subject: Jon Baker's +11 gross, the best gross round in TEG history to date, which delivered the TEG 7 Green Jacket lead by a single stroke while leaving him three adrift of Henry Meller in the TEG 7 Trophy
race_story.why_it_matters: The two competitions have opened with two different leaders, and Jon Baker's round is the lowest gross score anyone has returned in 101 TEG rounds — the Jacket race is one shot, the Trophy race three.
race_story.shape: Jon Baker takes a seven at the par-three 2nd, four over on a hole barely 200 yards long, and by then Henry Meller already has the Jacket lead. He claws it back all afternoon — level for the Jacket lead at the 12th, level for the Trophy lead at the 10th — and closes with three straight pars at the 16th, 17th and 18th for a gross +11, the best gross round TEG has seen. It gives him the Jacket by one from Meller and a -10 that is the third-best net round in TEG history, yet still three behind in the Trophy that matters most.
headline_candidates: Jon Baker's Record Gross Leads the Jacket
Jon Baker Recovers From a Seven
race_story.chosen_headline: Jon Baker's Record Gross Leads the Jacket
race_story.standfirst: He made a quadruple-bogey seven at the 2nd and still shot the lowest gross round in TEG history, which buys him a one-shot Jacket lead and precisely nothing in the Trophy.

discovered_storylines.subject: Alex Baker's first round of TEG golf: three eights, a quintuple bogey at the 5th, and last place in the TEG 7 Wooden Spoon race from the sixth hole onwards
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: It is his debut, it produced the worst score of the day at +1 net-vs-par against a field all in minus figures, and it has already opened a four-shot gap at the bottom of the Spoon race.
discovered_storylines.shape: He starts respectably enough, three bogeys in a row from the 2nd, and then takes an eight at the par-three 5th — five over, the worst he would manage against par all day. From the 6th he is bottom of the Spoon race and keeps confirming it: eleven shots bled between the 8th and the 11th, including another eight at the 10th, then a third eight at the 14th and eight more shots gone by the 16th. He signs for a gross 110 and a net +1, four clear of the field at the wrong end.
headline_candidates: Alex Baker Meets the Coastal Dunes
Three Eights and a Four-Shot Cushion
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Alex Baker's Debut Measured in Eights
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Three eights, one of them a quintuple bogey at a par three, and bottom of the Spoon race with seventeen holes still to play on his first day.

discovered_storylines.subject: Praia D'El Rey itself: a course new to every player in the field that handed out a quadruple bogey to four of the six and still let two records fall
discovered_storylines.why_it_matters: TEG's first visit to Portugal's Lisbon Coast produced both extremes on the same day, and the middle of the field spent the round trading blow-ups for recovery stretches.
discovered_storylines.shape: Nobody had played it, and the card showed it: David Mullin took eight at the closing par-four 18th, Gregg Williams eight at the 6th, Stuart Neumann triples at the 3rd and the 7th that dropped him to the bottom of the Spoon race twice before lunch. Yet the same holes rewarded patience — Williams answered with two separate four-hole runs of straight bogeys worth four shots to par apiece, and Mullin briefly held the outright Trophy lead at the 8th. The course finished the day having produced the best net round and the best gross round in TEG history alongside five scores of eight or worse.
headline_candidates: A New Course Takes Its Toll
Praia D'El Rey Sorts the Field
Four Quadruple Bogeys and Two Records
discovered_storylines.chosen_headline: Praia D'El Rey Sorts the Field
discovered_storylines.standfirst: Nobody in the field had seen the place before, and the dunes on the back nine collected an eight from four of the six men who walked them.

race_state_note: Round one of four, so these are openings rather than verdicts: Meller leads the Trophy by three from Jon Baker, Jon Baker leads the Jacket by one from Meller, and Alex Baker is four adrift of David Mullin and Stuart Neumann at the foot of the Spoon race.
